name: kick Ass order
caption: A recurring heel stable built around Mean Man and Basic Killer's SWL World Tag Team Titles reign, which absorbed Big Rob Styles and, by mid-1998, the newly turned World Champion Mass Destruction.

tenures.source: the fed's own Friday Night Raw (17 October 1997), served at /promotions/swl-1997b/archive/; the fed's own 1st Anniversary Friday Night Raw (13 March 1998), served at /promotions/swl-1997b/archive/; the fed's own newsletter The Archive, issue 1 (27 June 1998), served at /promotions/swl-1997b/archive/
tenures.notes: Membership evolves across this record: Mean Man and Basic Killer hold the SWL World Tag Team Titles from the earliest surviving card; Big Rob Styles's earlier turn is shown in the 1st Anniversary retrospective's own archival clips; Mass Destruction's turn is reported as recent news in the fed's own mid-1998 newsletter.

name: Elite-X
caption: A stable formed by Gravedigger, Jim Hart and Ryan Shaffer, announced as debuting on an uncollected episode of Wednesday Mayhem in the fed's own mid-1998 newsletter.

tenures.source: the fed's own newsletter The Archive, issue 1 (27 June 1998), served at /promotions/swl-1997b/archive/

name: Rebels of Apocalypse
caption: Insanity's own stable, entering him for his second SWL World Heavyweight Title reign and backing him, The Ruiner, The Executioner, Cassaday and Kraze through the promotion's Ring Masters broadcast.

tenures.source: the fed's own Ring Masters broadcast, 22 March 1998
tenures.notes: The broadcast's own commentary explicitly distinguishes this stable from an unrelated group of the same initials in a rival federation that Insanity was never part of.

name: The Dog House
caption: A trio of Chaos Bill, Tony Arnold and JunkYard who fought off a rival federation's debuting recruit on Ring Masters.

tenures.source: the fed's own Ring Masters broadcast, 22 March 1998

name: Natural Born Killers
caption: A stable naming Insanity and Gravedigger among its own members before Anthony Mislan is reported jumping ship from it to a new group, the Pain Killers.

tenures.source: the character's own self-posted broadcast parody, 29-30 March 1998; the fed's own newsletter The Archive, issue 1 (27 June 1998)
tenures.notes: Membership is inferred from a lower-formality, self-posted skit naming both wrestlers in the group and wearing its own t-shirt, corroborated by the fed's own newsletter reporting Anthony Mislan's departure from this same group; grade reflects that lower-formality sourcing.

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (nbk-chz); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.

name: Pain Killers
caption: The group Anthony Mislan is reported joining after leaving the Natural Born Killers, per the fed's own mid-1998 newsletter; billed at the Supremer Awards as formerly known as S.W.O. and led into the ring by Kraze, carrying the group's own Stable of the Year award.

tenures.source: the fed's own newsletter The Archive, issue 1 (27 June 1998); the fed's own Supremer Awards, 20 June 1998; the fed's own Warzone pay-per-view, 21 June 1998; the fed's own Monday Madness, 29 June 1998
tenures.notes: Won the fed's own Stable of the Year Supremer Award (20 June 1998) under this name, formerly S.W.O.; led by Kraze, who carries the group into both Warzone and Monday Madness.
